title: Azcuna v. Court of Appeals
summary: The Supreme Court ruled on the requirements for the probate of a will, holding that the probate court's role is limited to determining the due execution of the will and the testamentary capacity of the testator. Intrinsic validity of the will's provisions is examined only after probate.
doctrine: In probate proceedings, the court's authority is limited to determining: (1) whether the will was executed in accordance with the formalities prescribed by law; (2) whether the testator had testamentary capacity; and (3) whether the will was executed freely and voluntarily. The intrinsic validity of the provisions is not examined during probate.
fullText:
FRANCISCO, J.:

The issue is whether the lower court correctly disallowed the will offered for probate on the ground of undue influence.

In the probate of a will, the court's authority is limited to the extrinsic validity of the will — that is, whether the will was executed with the formalities required by law, whether the testator had testamentary capacity, and whether the will was executed free from force, duress, or undue influence.

The intrinsic validity of the testamentary provisions — such as the validity of the dispositions and the legality of the bequests — is to be passed upon only after the will has been admitted to probate.
